subject: POC runway safety net — capped burst credits vs. 2-week addendum
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@blueharbor.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@blueharbor.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC runway - we need a short-term safety net

Marcus —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Our team ran into a burst in inference during a data ingest test and we burned through about 40% of the POC capacity in 36 hours. We still need to evaluate the higher-concurrency flows for a production pass, but we don’t want to extend the full POC duration today.

Two asks: can you outline (a) a short-term safety-net that gives us extra burst capacity for the next 10 business days, and (b) an alternative that simply adds 2 full weeks to the POC window instead? We’re trying to decide which is cleaner from an internal procurement and usage-tracking perspective.

Procurement will need a price point and a simple amendment rather than a new contract. Also can you include whether either option changes SLA commitments for latency? We expect to stay on the same model we tested (rw-l7-large) and routing to us-west.

Attaching a small usage dump so you can see the burst pattern.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Director of ML Eng, BlueHarbor Systems
Attachment: blueharbor-usage-report-10-13.csv (csv)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC runway - we need a short-term safety net

Samira — thanks for the data and the clear ask. Quick summary below with two discrete options so procurement can sign an addendum without redoing the whole SOW.

Option A — Capped burst credits (preferred if you want a pay-as-burn guardrail):
- Deliverable: 150k token burst credit bucket usable over the next 10 business days.
- Price: $6,000 (one-time top-up).
- Mechanics: credits draw before incremental per-token billing; unused credits expire at midnight PT on the 10th business day.
- SLA: latency SLOs unchanged for hosted routing; if we hit sustained concurrent connections that require burst pool expansion, we’ll notify and propose fallback routing. This does not alter uptime SLA.

Option B — 2-week runway addendum (preferred if you want schedule certainty):
- Deliverable: extend POC end date by 14 calendar days and add a 40% higher concurrency allocation during that window.
- Price: $9,500 (flat addendum fee).
- Mechanics: will be added to your existing POC addendum; usage still measured and invoiced against normal per-token rates during the extension.
- SLA: same uptime and latency SLOs; higher concurrency window increases likelihood of transient throttling in extreme bursts — we recommend the capped-burst for unpredictable spikes.

Pricing rationale: capped credits give you predictable incremental spend for bursts; the extension buys calendar time and a temporary concurrency uplift. If procurement wants an alternative split (smaller credit bucket + 1-week extension) we can build that too.

Next steps I suggest: you confirm the preferred option and who in procurement will sign the addendum (email for DocuSign). I’ll prepare the addendum and loop legal for a one-paragraph change.

Attaching a short quote and a simple amendment template for procurement.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-topup-options-quote.pdf (pdf)
From: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@blueharbor.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira@blueharbor.com>
Cc: procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC runway - we need a short-term safety net

Marcus — appreciate the fast follow. A couple of procurement specifics from our side:
- Procurement prefers a one-off invoiceable line item (no credits that expire during a sprint unless we explicitly sign).
- If we can get the price for Option B down to ~7k we can sign today and add it as an amendment to the existing POC SOW.
- If you must keep Option A, can we do 100k tokens for $4k with a 14-day expiry instead of 10 business days? That might be acceptable.

Also, we need to confirm whether the extension triggers any changes to data handling (we are in a compliance window and need to ensure no additional logs are retained for longer than the POC retention policy).

If you can send a DocuSign link for the amendment and call out retention explicitly we’ll process it this week.

—Jorge
Jorge Alvarez
Senior Product Ops, BlueHarbor Systems
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@blueharbor.com>, Samira Khan <samira@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC runway - we need a short-term safety net

Jorge / Samira — thanks, good clarity. Quick responses inline and next steps below.

- Pricing / structure: we can do Option B (2-week addendum with concurrency uplift) at $7,000 and will include a one-line invoiceable addendum. That matches your ask and keeps accounting simple.

- Alternative credit: if you prefer the credit route we’ll offer 100k tokens for $4,000 with a 14-day expiry (instead of 10 business days). That gives you the burst headroom but with the short expiry you mentioned.

- Data retention / compliance: neither option changes default POC retention. We will add a clause in the addendum that re-states the POC log retention (30 days) and confirms no extra logs are ingested or retained by Redwood beyond the existing SOW. I’ll have Legal attach the clause to the amendment.

- SLA: no change. Latency and uptime SLOs remain as-is; the concurrency uplift is operational only and will be handled within the same regional routing.

Next steps (action items):
1) Confirm: Option B at $7,000 (2-week addendum) OR Option A credit 100k / $4,000 with 14-day expiry.
2) Tell us the procurement contact name and email to send DocuSign.
3) We will issue a one-line addendum + invoice and a DocuSign link within 4 business hours after confirmation.

For transparency I’ve cc’d Kimberly (legal liaison for addendums) and Dylan (solutions) if we need to tweak the concurrency window.

If you confirm by EOD tomorrow we’ll aim to get the amendment signed and applied before the weekend.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
